L01 - Python Variables, Data Types & Basic I/O (Week 1)
Lesson 1 Lecture Notes: Python Foundations.
Variables in Python are dynamically typed references to objects. Use type(x) to inspect types.
Common pitfall: concatenating str and int raises TypeError. Always cast with int() or str().
F-strings (Python 3.6+) evaluate expressions inside curly braces and support format specifiers.

L02 - Operators, Conditionals & Boolean Logic (Week 1)
Lesson 2 Lecture Notes: Control Flow.
Use == for value equality and = for assignment. Modulo % is essential for divisibility checks.
Truthy values: non-zero numbers, non-empty collections. Falsy: 0, '', [], {}, None, False.
Avoid deep nesting by using elif chains or early returns.

L03 - Loops, Iteration & Loop Control (Week 2)
Lesson 3 Lecture Notes: Iteration.
Infinite loops happen when the while condition never becomes False.
Use enumerate(seq) when you need both index and value instead of range(len(seq)).
Nested loops are used for 2D grids, multiplication tables, and pairwise comparisons.

L04 - Lists, Tuples, Indexing & Slicing (Week 2)
Lesson 4 Lecture Notes: Sequences.
Slicing creates a shallow copy: nums[:] copies the list.
Aliasing pitfall: b = a does NOT copy a list; both variables point to the same object.
Tuples cannot be modified in-place, preventing accidental mutation.

L05 - Dictionaries, Sets & Hashing (Week 3)
Lesson 5 Lecture Notes: Hash-based Structures.
Dictionary keys and set elements must be hashable (immutable types like int, str, tuple).
Use sets for fast membership testing (x in my_set) in O(1) average time vs O(n) for lists.

L06 - Functions, Scope & Recursion (Week 4)
Lesson 6 Lecture Notes: Functions & Recursion.
Never use mutable default arguments like def f(items=[]):; use None instead.
Every recursive function needs a base case to terminate and a recursive case that progresses toward it

L07 - Exceptions, File I/O & Comprehensions (Week 5)
Lesson 7 Lecture Notes: Robust Python & Pythonic Idioms.
Catch specific exceptions (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) rather than bare except:.
Generator expressions use parentheses (x*2 for x in data) and yield items on demand.

L08 - Object-Oriented Programming & Algorithmic Thinking (Week 6)
Lesson 8 Lecture Notes: OOP & Complexity.
__init__ initializes a newly created instance; __repr__ provides a developer-friendly string.
Binary search requires a sorted sequence and halves the search space each step.
